Runs 5–6 had killed `hour` and `video_type`/`music_type`/`tag` under the MLP on the five base fields. Since then both the model class (FM) and the feature set (rich causal sequences) changed, and an FM factorises every field pair — so the untested mechanism was the cross-field interactions (user×tag, tab×hour) a concat-MLP could never form. I ran a control arm on the identical code path so the verdict compares validation numbers from the same session, not across runs.

| Arm | valid | Δ vs control | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| control (FM-rich) | 0.61715 | — | 0.6098 ± 0.0010 |
| + hour | 0.61711 | −0.00004 | 0.6106 ± 0.0009 |
| + content | 0.61712 | −0.00003 | 0.6101 ± 0.0011 |
| + both | 0.61746 | +0.00031 | 0.6103 ± 0.0013 |

Best arm clears the control by a sixth of the 0.002 gate, so both ideas are marked DEAD and the pre-committed committee-promotion step did not fire. Banked best stays 0.6116; the `BANKED` constant in `harness.py` needed no change.

The interesting part is the *invariance*: Run 5 measured +0.0003 for these families under the MLP on base fields, and Run 30 measures +0.0003 under the FM on rich causal fields. Two model classes and two feature regimes apart, the number doesn't budge — that argues the fields genuinely carry no incremental within-user ranking signal, rather than that the earlier architecture was too weak to exploit them.

Also recorded a third test-peek refusal: R30a's test (0.6106) sits +0.0008 above the control while its validation is 0.00004 *below* it. Logged as an observation, not a result.

Committed as `aaa5ef3` and pushed to both remotes. Remaining OPEN: #12 duration-normalised play-ratio, #13 K=2 under FM-rich, #14 per-field embedding sizes.

ITERATION RESULT: Run 30 side+content fields under FM-rich | 0.6103 | NOT_BANKED | hour and content metadata add +0.0003 under the FM on rich features — the exact same margin Run 5 found under the MLP on base fields, so the fields, not the architecture, are the limit.
